Controls and Procedures (a) Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures The company’s management has evaluated, with the participation of the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, the effectiveness of the company’s disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act)) as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on this evaluation, management concluded that the company’s disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December 31, 2025. (b) Management’s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting The company’s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as defined in the Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f). The company’s management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of the company’s internal control over financial reporting based on the Internal Control – Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). Based on the results of this evaluation, the company’s management concluded that internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2025. The company excluded Hess from our assessment of internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, because it was acquired by the company in a business combination during 2025. Total assets and total revenues of Hess, a 30 Table of Contents wholly-owned subsidiary of Chevron Corporation, represent 24 percent and 3 percent, respectively, of the related consolidated financial statement amounts as of and for the period ended December 31, 2025. The effectiveness of the company’s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in its report included herein. (c) Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting During the quarter ended December 31, 2025, there were no changes in the company’s internal control over financial reporting that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the company’s internal control over financial reporting. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital spending plus dividends, and also covers dividends and buybacks combined, so the upstream and refining cash engine funds both reinvestment and shareholder returns without new borrowing.
Interest coverage sits far above the sector median and EBITDA coverage is roughly triple the peer median, reflecting a low-cost debt stack and modest coupon burden relative to earnings power.

key_risks.text: Gross and net leverage both rose sharply year over year as debt increased to fund the Hess acquisition, and the acquired entity was excluded from internal control assessment, so integration and purchase accounting remain unproven.

Free cash flow falls short of total dividends plus buybacks, meaning distributions are partly funded from balance-sheet capacity rather than internally generated cash, a structural reliance if commodity prices weaken.

The debt note shows a heavy near-term maturity wall, with notes due in the second and third years and a large reclassified short-term balance, concentrating refinancing risk in a rising-rate environment.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating income covers interest expense many times over, and the debt note confirms a weighted-average coupon in the low single digits, so scheduled interest is easily absorbed even under a weaker margin environment.

Free cash flow to debt exceeds the sector median and cash flow to debt is marginally above peers, though both ratios declined year over year, indicating servicing headroom is narrowing as leverage builds.

overall_credit_view.text: Net leverage remains below the sector median and well inside the next risk-band boundary, and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal, so the balance sheet retains meaningful capacity to absorb commodity cyclicality.

Operating margin trails the sector median and weakened year over year, so the credit view rests on scale and balance-sheet strength rather than margin leadership; continued distribution funding from debt would erode that cushion.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健覆蓋資本開支加股息，亦覆蓋股息與回購之總和，因此上游及煉油現金引擎可在無新增借貸下同時支持再投資與股東回報。
利息覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，而 EBITDA 覆蓋率約為同業中位數之三倍，反映低成本債務結構及相對於盈利能力而言溫和的票息負擔。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿及淨槓桿均按年大幅上升，因債務增加以撥付 Hess 收購，且被收購實體未納入內部控制評估，故整合及購買會計處理仍屬未經證實。
自由現金流不足以覆蓋股息加回購總額，意味分派部分由資產負債表能力而非內部產生現金撥付，若商品價格轉弱則屬結構性依賴。
債務附註顯示沉重的近期到期牆，第二及第三年到期票據加上大額重分類短期結餘，將再融資風險集中於利率上升環境。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營溢利覆蓋利息開支多倍，且債務附註確認加權平均票息處於低單位數，故即使利潤率環境轉弱，預定利息仍易於吸收。
自由現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，現金流對債務比率略高於同業，惟兩項比率均按年下降，顯示隨著槓桿累積，償債空間正在收窄。

overall_credit_view.text: 淨槓桿仍低於行業中位數，且遠在下一風險區間邊界之內，而指示性財務風險狀況為極低，故資產負債表仍保有可觀能力吸收商品週期性波動。
經營利潤率低於行業中位數並按年轉弱，故信用觀點依賴規模及資產負債表實力而非利潤率領先地位；若持續以債務撥付分派，將侵蝕該緩衝。
